# Offensive Security Intro — Active Recall

**Platform:** TryHackMe  
**Method:** Questions generated by AI; answers written independently from
memory without consulting the lesson or AI-generated answers.

## Initial recall

### 1. What is offensive security?

> Offensive security is exploiting vulnerabilities or breaching security so
> that you can get your mind to think in the way of a malicious hacker.

**Result:** Mostly correct

### 2. What did you do to the FakeBank website?

> I don't remember the name of the command, but I remember it gave me all the
> hidden links connected to the main website. I used one to access FakeBank's
> admin controls and send myself money.

**Result:** Correct process; tool name missing

### 3. What security mistake made the attack possible?

> Allowing regular individuals access to an admin portion of the website.

**Result:** Correct

## Follow-up questions

### 4. What separates an ethical hacker from a malicious hacker?

> The intent. Ethical hackers breach systems to understand vulnerabilities and
> prevent them from happening. Malicious hackers breach systems to take
> advantage of vulnerabilities and obtain some sort of gain.

**Result:** Partially correct—authorization is the key distinction

### 5. What was `dirb` discovering?

> Dirb was discovering hidden websites.

**Result:** Partially correct—pages and directories within a website

### 6. Would good intentions alone make unauthorized hacking ethical?

> No, the company never gave them the authorization to hack regardless of what
> their intentions were.

**Result:** Correct

### 7. What should prevent ordinary users from using an admin page?

> Access control.

**Result:** Correct

## Corrections retained

- Ethical hacking requires explicit authorization and an agreed scope.
- `dirb` enumerates accessible pages and directories on a website.
- Hidden URLs do not replace server-side access control.

**Final understanding:** Ready to move on
